title: Optimized Lévy distance bound
statement: Let $m$ be a nonnegative integer and let $mu,nu$ be probability measures on $bbr$. Define their Lévy distance as the infimum of all $deltage0$ such that, for every $uinbbr$, $(nu((-infty,u-delta]).toReal-delta)lemu((-infty,u]).toReal$ and $mu((-infty,u]).toReallenu((-infty,u+delta]).toReal+delta$. Suppose $Bge0$ and, for every $(m+1)$ times continuously differentiable function $phi:bbrtobbr$, every $Cge0$ bounding $|phi^{(m+1)}(t)|$ for all $t$, the absolute difference between the integrals of $phi$ against $mu$ and $nu$ is at most $CB$. Then the Lévy distance is at most $((m+2)+2^m)B^{1/(m+2)}$.
